methodology_note: Live network access to asu-aramark.netlify.app and Supabase's raw REST endpoint is blocked at the sandbox's egress policy level for this session (confirmed via curl, playwright-cli, and WebFetch — all independently hit the same policy denial). Tests marked 'code_trace' were verified by reading the exact source function in index.html. Tests marked 'data_verified' were verified by replaying the app's actual query filters as SQL via the Supabase MCP connector (a separate, working access path) against real or QA-tagged (is_test=true) data. Tests marked BLOCKED require live browser interaction and could not be run from this sandbox.

tests.actual: FOUND BUG: fallback only pushed to role=warehouse_employee. FIXED this session (build 2026-09-27-stock-fallback-notify-1) — now includes warehouse_supervisor and warehouse_manager.

tests.feature: Delivery-ready-to-verify push when no supervisor is on shift

tests.feature: Overdue stock ETA escalation targets the right person

tests.feature: All-stands / My Team counts must show full game roster, not just current shift block
tests.steps: Trace getBedCheck() and getMyTeam(); check real schedule data for multi-shift-block stands.
tests.expected: 207 with 30 scheduled across multiple shift-start times shows 30, not just whoever's shift has started.
tests.actual: Verified already fixed in a prior build (in-code comments document the exact '3-vs-8 mismatch' bug and its fix). Both getBedCheck (Team Control) and getMyTeam (Stand Lead roster) dedupe by employee_id with NO shift-time-window filtering. Confirmed via Supabase that a real game's 207 crew spans 4 different start times (11:00/13:00/15:00/15:30) in one crew, exactly the shape that would break a shift-filtered version.
tests.evidence: index.html ~L5439-5482 (getBedCheck), ~L5596-5643 (getMyTeam); Supabase query on schedule for 207 on 2026-09-05

tests.feature: Move worker between stands uses a real picker, not a numbered prompt()
tests.expected: A real searchable stand-picker modal, matching the spec's explicit 'DO NOT use a giant numbered JavaScript prompt' requirement.
tests.actual: Confirmed already fixed in a prior build — in-code comment documents replacing a 47+-item numbered prompt() with populateStandPicker() modal.

tests.feature: Move worker updates both location AND crew/event_name
tests.expected: Destination Stand Lead (crew-scoped) sees the worker after move; old Stand Lead does not.
tests.actual: Confirmed: PATCH sets both location and, when a matching destination crew is found, event_name. Since getMyTeam filters by event_name for Stand Leads, this correctly moves the worker's crew membership, not just their location label.

tests.feature: Move/walk-in event_name resolution when destination stand has ambiguous crew names
tests.steps: Built a synthetic duplicate schedule on a safe, non-colliding test date (2000-01-01, never matches any real 'today' query) via the Supabase MCP connector, including a stand with two crews sharing one location where neither event_name matches the '<3-digit> Stand' regex pattern. Replayed managerMoveWorker's and addWalkin's exact resolution logic as SQL against it.
tests.expected: The code should not silently guess which crew to attach the worker to.
tests.actual: CONFIRMED REAL BUG, reproduced concretely (not hypothetical): the code picked whichever crew name came back first with zero indication of ambiguity — a moved/walked-in worker could land in the wrong Stand Lead's roster silently. FIXED this session (build 2026-09-27-crew-ambiguity-fix-1): when ambiguous, Move Worker leaves crew grouping unset instead of guessing (still visible in the location-based Team Control overview) and Add Walk-in falls back to its own walk-in crew group (the same fallback already used for a stand with no crew at all); both now show the acting manager an explicit warning toast instead of failing silently. All synthetic test data was on the 2000-01-01 test date only and has been fully deleted (verified: 0 rows remaining) — no real schedule data was touched.
tests.method: data_verified (synthetic QA dataset, cleaned up after)

tests.feature: Duplicate-import resilience: same employee appearing twice in one crew's schedule
tests.steps: Inserted the same employee_id twice under the same event_name with two different start_times (mirrors a real documented ReadyOn duplicate-import scenario) into the synthetic dataset above, then replayed getMyTeam's and getBedCheck's exact dedup algorithm as SQL.
tests.expected: Dedupes to one person, keeping the earliest start_time, at both the crew level and the location level.
tests.actual: Confirmed correct in both cases — 29 (crew) and 32 (full location, including a second unrelated crew) came back exactly as expected, duplicate correctly collapsed to its earliest-start-time row.
tests.method: data_verified (synthetic QA dataset, cleaned up after)
tests.evidence: SQL replication of schedule dedup logic against test date 2000-01-01, deleted after

tests.feature: Duplicate-submission protection (client_uuid) actually enforced at the DB level, not just assumed by app code
tests.steps: Attempted to insert two stock_requests rows with the identical client_uuid in one transaction.
tests.expected: Second insert rejected; first insert not silently duplicated.
tests.actual: Confirmed: unique index uq_stock_requests_client_uuid (and the equivalent for kitchen_requests) rejected the duplicate with a real constraint violation; the whole test transaction rolled back cleanly, leaving zero rows behind.
tests.evidence: Postgres error 23505 on uq_stock_requests_client_uuid; verified 0 rows left in stock_requests for the QA-TEST-STAND probe

tests.feature: Walk-in does not create a duplicate person if already scheduled today
tests.expected: If employee already has a schedule row today, reject with 'use Move stand' rather than creating a second row.
tests.actual: Confirmed: queries schedule for existing row matching the same 5-digit suffix before insert; blocks with explicit message if found.

tests.feature: Walk-in accepts 5-digit login ID or full 8-digit employee ID

tests.feature: BUILD_TAG / sw.js version match, no-cache headers, no refresh loop
tests.steps: Check _headers file and BUILD_TAG/sw.js version constant in source; live verification needs the deployed site.
tests.expected: index.html and sw.js are no-cache; BUILD_TAG shown on login footer matches deployed build.
tests.actual: Confirmed: _headers sets Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate for both /index.html and /sw.js, so the CDN and browser never cache either file — that structurally prevents the 'stale saved app version' failure mode regardless of sw.js's own CACHE_VERSION constant (which only affects secondary cached assets like icons, not these two). Live confirmation of the BUILD_TAG shown on the actual login footer still needs a live browser (blocked).
